comments.headline: Transformer pad building clearances not documented
comments.summary: Clearances from transformer pads to buildings, balconies, overhangs, and building openings (windows, doors, ducts) are not dimensioned or verified on the electrical plan. Required Austin Energy Design approvals for reduced clearances are not provided.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy Design may require written approvals if reduced clearances are proposed.
comments.attn: Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) must be specified to determine correct clearance requirements. Building elevations must be coordinated with transformer pad locations.

details.text: Clearance dimensions between transformer pads and adjacent buildings are not specified. Compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan but no clearance dimensions are specified between any transformer pad and adjacent buildings. Clearance compliance cannot be verified from the submitted plans.

details.text: Plans do not indicate if reduced 3-foot clearances are proposed for any transformer location. If reduced clearances are used, Austin Energy Design written approval and documentation of required conditions (not in confined space, 10+ ft to windows/doors/ducts, 15+ ft vertical clearance, 3-hour fire rating) are missing.

runComments.comment: Plans do not indicate whether any transformer pads have clearances less than 5 feet to buildings. If reduced clearances (3 feet) are proposed, no Austin Energy Design written approval or documentation of required conditions (not in confined space, 10 ft+ to windows/doors/ducts, 15 ft+ vertical clearance, 3-hour fire rating) is provided.

details.text: Clearances from transformer pads to building balconies and overhangs are not dimensioned or verified. No vertical clearance drawings confirm that pads are not covered by overhead structures and maintain minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from balconies.

runComments.comment: Buildings have balconies and overhangs shown on site plan. No clearance dimensions or vertical clearance drawings verify that transformer pads have minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from balconies and are not covered by overhead structures.

details.text: Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified. Clearance from windows/doors/ducts requiring 12-foot horizontal clearance for oil-filled equipment is not documented. No building elevations coordinate with transformer pad locations to verify clearances.

runComments.comment: Clearance from windows/doors/ventilating ducts requires 12-foot horizontal clearance for oil-filled equipment (if window/door/duct is less than 12 feet from grade or has less than 5 feet lateral separation). Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified, and no building elevations coordinate with transformer pad locations to verify clearances.

comments.headline: Transformer pad clearances to site elements not verified
comments.summary: Clearances from transformer pads to retaining walls, fences, sidewalks, fire hydrants, dumpsters, bike racks, light poles, fire lanes, and spacing between pads are not dimensioned or coordinated on the electrical and site plans.
comments.crossDep: Fire Department (fire hydrant, fire lanes); Landscape/Site Design (bike racks, dumpster, light poles); Civil/Grading (retaining walls, sidewalks)
comments.attn: Verify exact spacing requirements for each element type with Austin Energy Design. Fire lane clearance (15 feet) differs from other site elements (5 feet).

details.text: Retaining wall locations (Sheet 11) are not clearly coordinated with transformer pad locations (Sheet 21). No clearance dimensions are shown between transformer pads and retaining walls.

runComments.comment: Retaining walls are shown on the grading plan (Sheet 11) but their location relative to transformer pads on Sheet 21 is not clearly coordinated. No clearance dimensions are shown between transformer pads and retaining walls.

details.text: Property boundary fences shown on site plan lack dimension callouts verifying clearance from transformer pads. Required 5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3 feet for removable ventilated fences cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Site plan shows property boundary fences but no dimension callouts verify clearance from transformer pads to fences (required 5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3 feet for other sides with removable ventilated fences).

details.text: Sidewalks near transformer pad locations lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalk to pad.

runComments.comment: Site plan shows sidewalks near some transformer pad locations, but no dimension callouts verify the minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalk to transformer pad.

details.text: Private fire hydrant location (Sheet 10) is not coordinated or dimensioned relative to transformer pads on electrical plan. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: One private fire hydrant is shown on the site plan (Sheet 10). Its location relative to any transformer pads is not coordinated or dimensioned on either the fire protection plan or electrical plan. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

details.text: Dumpster enclosure location shown on site plan is not dimensioned relative to transformer pads. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Site plan shows dumpster enclosure location but does not coordinate or dimension clearance from transformer pads. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

details.text: Bike rack locations (41 spaces in parking areas) are not coordinated or dimensioned relative to transformer pads. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Site plan shows bike rack locations (41 spaces provided in parking areas) but does not coordinate or dimension clearance from transformer pads. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

details.text: Light pole locations are not documented or coordinated with transformer pad locations. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Light pole locations would be shown on photometric/site lighting plan but no coordination is documented with transformer pad locations. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

details.text: Fire lane locations (Sheet 10) are not dimensioned relative to transformer pads on electrical plan. Minimum 15-foot clearance from fire lanes cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Fire protection plan (Sheet 10) shows fire lanes on site but coordination with transformer pad locations is not dimensioned. Minimum 15-foot clearance from fire lanes cannot be verified.

details.text: Five transformer pads shown on electrical plan lack dimension callouts verifying spacing between pads. Minimum 5-foot clearance between transformer pads cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Five transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan but no dimension callouts verify spacing between pads. Minimum 5-foot clearance between transformer pads cannot be verified.

comments.headline: Transformer pad operational space clearances not documented
comments.summary: Hot-stick use areas, confined space clearances, fire escape coordination, and stairwell relationships are not documented on the electrical plan. Required operational clearances cannot be verified.
comments.attn: Access door orientation and hot-stick use area (10-foot minimum from access door) must be clearly marked on electrical plan. Confirm whether any pads are located in confined spaces (niches, vaults, or enclosed areas on 3+ sides).

details.text: Hot-stick use area clearance (minimum 10 feet from access door side) is not documented. Electrical plan shows transformer locations but does not document access door orientation or clearances to open areas or adjacent structures.

runComments.comment: Hot-stick use area clearance (minimum 10 feet from access door side) is a fundamental requirement for all transformer pads. The electrical plan shows transformer locations but does not document access door orientation or clearances to open areas or adjacent structures.

details.text: Increased 15-foot clearance requirement for confined spaces is not addressed. Plans do not identify whether any transformer locations are in confined spaces or provide cross-section drawings demonstrating 15-foot clearance within enclosed areas.

runComments.comment: Increased clearance requirement (15 feet) applies only if transformer location faces confined space (niche, vault, or enclosed area on 3+ sides). Plans do not clearly identify whether any transformer locations are in confined spaces or provide cross-section drawings demonstrating 15-foot clearance within enclosed areas.

details.text: Building floor plans showing stairwell locations have not been reviewed. Relationship between transformer pad locations and any exterior stairwells is not documented on electrical or site plan.

runComments.comment: Building floor plans would show stairwell locations but have not been reviewed. Relationship between transformer pad locations and any exterior stairwells is not documented on the electrical or site plan.

details.text: Fire escape locations (Sheet 10) are not clearly coordinated with transformer pad locations. Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified. 20-foot clearance requirement for oil-filled equipment cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Fire protection plan (Sheet 10) shows fire hydrants but fire escape locations are not clearly coordinated with transformer pad locations on electrical plan. Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified. 20-foot clearance requirement for oil-filled equipment cannot be verified.

comments.headline: Utility line clearances from transformer pads not coordinated
comments.summary: Clearances from transformer pads to water, wastewater, storm sewer, and other underground utilities are not dimensioned. Underground utility cross-section documentation is missing.
comments.crossDep: Water Utility; Wastewater Utility; Stormwater/Watershed Management
comments.attn: 5-foot clearance required from transformer pads to water/wastewater/storm lines per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2. 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance required from other underground utilities per UCM § 1.10.5.A.

details.text: Water line routing (Sheet 19) is shown but dimension callouts do not verify minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to water service lines.

runComments.comment: Utility plans show water line routing but no dimension callouts verify the minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to water lines.

details.text: Wastewater line routing (Sheet 19) is shown but dimension callouts do not verify minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to wastewater service lines.

runComments.comment: Utility plans show wastewater line routing but no dimension callouts verify the minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to wastewater lines.

details.text: Storm drain line routing (Sheet 12) is shown but dimension callouts do not verify minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines.

runComments.comment: Storm sewer plan (Sheet 12) shows drainage infrastructure but no dimension callouts verify minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines.

details.text: Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities is not dimensioned. No clearance callouts verify this clearance from transformer pads to any underground utilities (power conduits, telecommunications, etc.).

runComments.comment: Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities is a fundamental requirement. No dimension callouts on the electrical plan verify this clearance from transformer pads to any underground utilities (power conduits, telecommunications, etc.).

details.text: Cross-section drawings or coordination notes documenting that transformer pads are not located over/under other utility lines, and that customer buildings are not installed over AE underground facilities, are missing.

runComments.comment: Plans do not clearly document that transformer pads or AE underground facilities are not located over/under other utility lines, or that customer buildings/foundations/structures are not installed over AE underground facilities. Cross-section drawings or detailed coordination notes are needed.

comments.headline: Overhead distribution clearances and cross-sections not documented
comments.summary: Vertical and horizontal clearances from overhead distribution lines are not dimensioned. Cross-section drawings showing overhead line clearances and customer facilities are missing.
comments.attn: 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius clearance (measured from conductors, not pole centerline) are required per UCM § 1.10.3. Cross-section drawings must show vertical clearances in access paths and enclosed areas.

details.text: Overhead distribution lines shown on utility plans lack vertical clearance drawings or dimension callouts verifying minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors at transformer pad locations.

runComments.comment: Overhead distribution lines are shown on utility plans but no vertical clearance drawings or dimension callouts verify the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors extending from ground to sky at transformer pad locations.

details.text: Overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors shown on electrical plan lack dimension callouts verifying 15-foot radius clearance measured from conductors (not pole centerline) at transformer pad locations.

runComments.comment: Overhead distribution lines are shown on electrical plan but no dimension callouts or measurements verify the 15-foot radius clearance from conductors (measured from conductors, not pole centerline) at transformer pad locations.

details.text: No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances in access paths, overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas at transformer pad locations. Cross-sections are required to demonstrate hot-stick use area and overhead obstruction compliance.
details.citation: UCM § 1.10.3 (survey requirement as required by AE Design)

runComments.comment: No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances in access paths, overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas at transformer pad locations. Cross-sections are required to demonstrate vertical clearance compliance, especially for hot-stick use areas and overhead obstructions.

details.text: Overhead distribution facilities shown on utility plans lack cross-section documentation verifying that customer facilities (buildings, parking structures, light poles, signs, antennas, tanks) are not installed under or over overhead lines.

runComments.comment: Overhead distribution facilities are shown on utility plans but cross-section documentation verifying that customer facilities (buildings, parking structures, light poles, signs, antennas, tanks) are not installed under or over these lines is not provided. Coordinate cross-sections or clearance notes are needed.

comments.headline: Transformer pad design specifications and easement documentation incomplete
comments.summary: Transformer pad dimensions, service type, equipment specifications, and location on private property are not documented. Required transformer easements and protective bollards are not shown. Electrical routing and easement conflicts are not verified.
comments.crossDep: Civil/Grading (easement exhibit); Austin Energy Design (pad detail approval)
comments.attn: Transformer pad detail sheets must be obtained from Austin Energy Design. Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) and service configuration (single-phase vs. three-phase) must be specified to determine pad size and easement requirements. Verify all transformer locations are 100% on private property.

details.text: Transformer pad dimensions and service type are not specified. No dimension callouts show pad sizes, and no references to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets for specified service type are provided.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad dimensions are NOT specified on the electrical plan. No dimension callouts show pad sizes (e.g., 5'x5', 10'x10', etc.), and no references are provided to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase). Service type is not documented. Pad dimensions must be verified against AE Design standards.

details.text: Transformer pads must be located 100% on private property, not in public right-of-way or straddling property lines. Transformer pad locations are not dimensioned or verified relative to property boundary lines on electrical or site plan.

runComments.comment: Requirement that transformer pads be located 100% on private property, not in public right-of-way or straddling property lines, is not explicitly verified on the electrical or site plan. Transformer pad locations relative to property boundary lines are not dimensioned or documented.

details.text: Transformer pads must not be located in prohibited easements (drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements under overhead lines) without Austin Energy Design approval. Transformer pad locations are shown on electrical plan but NOT shown on grading plan easement exhibit, preventing verification of easement conflicts.

runComments.comment: Transformer pads must not be located in prohibited easements (drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements under overhead lines) without AE Design written approval. Transformer pad locations are shown on the electrical plan but NOT shown on the grading plan easement exhibit, preventing verification of easement conflicts. Easements are shown on the grading plan but transformer locations are not coordinated with easement boundaries.

details.text: Transformer easements are not shown around any transformer pad locations. While a general note states additional electric easements may be required, preliminary electrical plan does not show transformer-specific easements with widths specified for Austin Energy accessibility requirements.

runComments.comment: Transformer easements are NOT shown around any transformer pad locations. While a note on Sheet 9 states 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' the preliminary electrical plan does not show transformer-specific easements with specified widths for Austin Energy accessibility requirements. Easement boundaries and widths must be documented on the site plan.

details.text: Electrical routing from transformer to meter must be 100% on private property. Electrical plan shows routing paths but does not explicitly verify or document that entire path is on private property, not crossing right-of-way or easements.

runComments.comment: Electrical routing from transformer to meter must be 100% on private property. The electrical plan shows routing paths but does not explicitly verify or document that the entire path is on private property, not crossing right-of-way or easements.

details.text: Transformer pads located within 4 feet of parking aisles or vehicle circulation routes require 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards per Austin Energy Design pad details. No bollard specifications or details are shown on site plan or detail sheets.

runComments.comment: Transformer pads are located within or immediately adjacent to parking areas on the site plan. Where pads are within 4 feet of parking aisles or vehicle circulation routes, 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards are required per AE Design equipment pad details. No bollard specifications or details are shown on the site plan or detail sheets.

details.text: Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on electrical plan. Grading plan shows general surface drainage, but specific documentation that drainage from transformer pad locations slopes away from buildings (required for oil-filled equipment) is not provided.

runComments.comment: Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on the electrical plan. Grading plan shows general surface drainage flowing downhill away from buildings, but specific documentation that drainage from transformer pad locations slopes away from buildings (required for oil-filled equipment) is not provided.
